taglines: It is Wednesday, which is the geographical center of the work week. You are equidistant from both weekends. Neither one can help you now. You are precisely in the middle of the problem.
Hump Day implies you are climbing something and the other side is easier. No one has confirmed what is on the other side. For all anyone knows it is just more hump.

You have a recurring meeting every Wednesday at 2pm to discuss priorities. The priorities have not changed since March. The meeting persists. The meeting has outlasted three different 'priority frameworks.' The meeting is the priority.
Someone sent a message that said 'per my last email' and everyone understood immediately that a crime had been committed against them, documented, and filed.
The AI wrote your first draft. You edited it for twenty minutes to sound more like you. You then sent the version that sounded less like you. This is fine. This is the process now.

There are 23 productivity apps on your phone. Combined they have saved you zero hours. You have spent eleven hours across them logging the time you are saving. The math does not close and you know it.

Somewhere there is a version of you who finished the project on the original deadline. That version lives in a timeline where the scope never changed and stakeholders responded to Slack. That version is a myth. A beautiful, unreachable myth.
Wednesday is proof that you can want Friday very badly and still have more than two days left. Desire does not accelerate time. The calendar is indifferent to your feelings about it.
